name: Runtime workflow and delivery
observations: OpenMontage documents an agent-first workflow: the agent reads a YAML pipeline manifest and stage skill, calls Python tools, self-reviews, checkpoints JSON state, obtains approval, runs pre-compose validation, renders with Remotion or FFmpeg, performs post-render self-review, and presents the final video only if review passes (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/README.md:393-431).

The documented quality gates include human approval at proposal/script/scene-plan/assets/publish stages, pre-compose delivery-promise and slideshow-risk validation, post-render ffprobe plus four-position frame extraction plus audio analysis plus subtitle/promise checks, and blocking presentation when review fails (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/README.md:637-647).

Runtime selection is explicitly locked in proposal as render_runtime and carried through edit_decisions; silent runtime swaps are described as governance violations (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/README.md:592-600).

The Remotion package exposes studio, a fixed Explainer render command to out/video.mp4, and upgrade scripts; dependencies include Remotion CLI, React, transitions, media, captions, and Google Fonts (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/package.json:1-31).

The checked-in demo wrapper is fail-fast (set -euo pipefail), resolves its own directory, and delegates to render_demo.py with Python 3 when available (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/render-demo.sh:1-10). The Python demo validates that each props file has a nonempty cuts list, installs npm dependencies if node_modules is absent, renders Remotion Explainer with H.264, and writes demos under projects/demos/renders/<name>.mp4 (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/render_demo.py:49-108).

OpenMontage's render_report contract requires version 1.0 and at least one output with path, format, resolution, and duration_seconds; optional fields cover codecs, fps, file size, platform target, warnings, verification notes, render grammar, slideshow risk, decision-log reference, and final-review reference (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/schemas/artifacts/render_report.schema.json:3-62).

The final_review contract requires output_path, pass/revise/fail status, and technical, visual, audio, promise-preservation, and subtitle checks. Visual checks require at least four sampled frames; promise checks record actual renderer/runtime, runtime swaps, motion ratio, and silent downgrades; recommended actions include present, re-render, revise, block, and re-author (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/schemas/artifacts/final_review.schema.json:3-17,19-119,157-169).

Publishing is modeled as a separate PUBLISH-tier local tool. export_bundle requires video_path and title, rejects missing video and explicitly supplied missing subtitle/thumbnail files, copies the video and optional assets, writes metadata/description/tags/chapters and thumbnail artifacts, and returns a schema-validated publish_log (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/tools/publishers/export_bundle.py:39-127,158-199,207-285).

The default export layout is projects/<name>/exports when the render is projects/<name>/renders/...; otherwise it falls back to exports/<project_name> (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/tools/publishers/export_bundle.py:287-307). The publish log status is exported, not network-published; the tool declares no network requirement and uploads=false (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/tools/publishers/export_bundle.py:50-69,251-275).

The publish_log schema requires version 1.0 and entries with platform, status, and date-time timestamp; allowed statuses include published, exported, failed, draft, and pending_review (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/schemas/artifacts/publish_log.schema.json:3-39).

OpenMontage tests verify export bundle layout, subtitle and thumbnail handling, chapter formatting, schema-valid publish logs, missing-video errors, missing optional-asset errors, project-local default export location, and registry discovery (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/tests/tools/test_export_bundle.py:1-5,27-45,47-98,126-155).

MPS MPVE accepts a structured VideoRequest with topic/objective, learning context, duration 15-45 seconds, fixed 16:9 aspect ratio, optional analogy consent, and derived=true enforcement for FHP mode (/home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:26-85).

MPS creates an in-memory job index with SHA-256 request fingerprints for deduplication, persists each job as job.json, runs planning/rendering in a daemon thread, writes storyboard.json, renders video.mp4, writes render.manifest.json, and records artifact/provider/audio/fallback/quality-gate metadata in the job result (/home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:131-177,180-228).

MPS exposes POST /videos plus GET /videos/{job_id} and GET /videos/{job_id}/result; duplicate submissions return 200, new submissions 202, non-completed result requests return 409, and missing jobs return 404 (/home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/mpve_server.py:1-8,33-65).

MPS's hybrid renderer tries local Pillow/FFmpeg, then an optional hosted adapter, then SVG fallback. Local output is H.264/yuv420p with faststart; fallback returns no MP4 path but does generate SVG assets (/home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:1-12,183-214,216-251).

MPS's production manifest records provider order, render_runtime=python-ffmpeg, required tools ffmpeg/ffprobe, and named quality gates, but the manifest is a JSON artifact written by the pipeline rather than a demonstrated canonical schema validator (/home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/production_manifest.py:19-79).

MPS tests cover request rejection, FHP derivation gating, idempotent duplicate jobs, successful artifact/storyboard presence, and renderer exception propagation (/home/ubuntu/MPS-git/tests/test_mpve.py:11-79).
inferences: OpenMontage treats delivery as a gated, auditable state transition rather than merely writing an MP4: proposal decisions, checkpoints, render report, final review, and publish log form a durable evidence chain.

OpenMontage separates composition/rendering from delivery packaging: the render report and final review describe whether an output is safe to present, while export_bundle creates a hand-off package without claiming platform upload.

The OpenMontage contracts are designed to support multiple runtimes and platform targets, whereas the current MPS vertical slice is intentionally a single local-first cinematic MPVE path with one fixed aspect ratio and a provider fallback ladder.

MPS's asynchronous job API is the delivery boundary currently exposed to callers; its durable per-job files make artifacts addressable, but the authoritative job index and deduplication map are process-local.

MPS's named quality gates are partly declarative: the current code verifies storyboard validity and output existence, but it does not visibly execute the OpenMontage-style ffprobe, four-frame, audio, subtitle, delivery-promise, or runtime-swap review contract before completing a job.

The MPS fallback behavior intentionally treats SVG-only fallback as failed for MPVE completion because MPVE requires result.output_path to exist, even though the lower-level renderer reports generated fallback assets.
unknowns: The inspected OpenMontage files do not by themselves prove the exact production invocation path that connects every pipeline's compose output to export_bundle; the README describes the workflow, but a single end-to-end publish runner was not identified in this scoped inspection.

It is not established from the inspected OpenMontage runtime files whether all documented human approval gates are enforced by every pipeline implementation or only by shared checkpoint infrastructure and policy.
The exact contents and first-party usage of project-local props, assets, and generated render reports across all Remotion compositions are not uniform from the README/package files alone.
MPS persistence across process restart, recovery of daemon threads, and cross-process idempotency are not established; the code only shows in-memory indexes plus per-job JSON writes.
MPS's current working tree reports modifications to README.md and scripts/logic_engine.py; their changes were outside this subsystem, so their impact on the inspected MPVE runtime is unknown.
No MPS publisher/export-bundle endpoint, publish_log artifact, subtitle package, thumbnail package, or platform upload implementation was found in the inspected runtime files.
contracts: A render completion contract should expose at least a concrete output path plus format/resolution/duration and should retain warnings and verification references; OpenMontage formalizes this in render_report version 1.0 (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/schemas/artifacts/render_report.schema.json:7-30).
A presented output must have final_review status pass; revise/fail outcomes must not be presented as complete (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/schemas/artifacts/final_review.schema.json:3-7,14-17).

Post-render evidence must include technical probing, opening/middle/climax/ending visual samples (minimum four), audio checks, delivery-promise/runtime governance checks, and subtitle verification (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/schemas/artifacts/final_review.schema.json:19-119).

The runtime actually executed must be recorded and compared to the runtime locked at proposal; unapproved runtime swaps and silent downgrades are violations (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/schemas/artifacts/final_review.schema.json:80-105; /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/README.md:596-600).

A publish/export result must be represented as a version-1.0 publish_log entry with platform, allowed status, and ISO date-time timestamp; local export is distinct from remote publication (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/schemas/artifacts/publish_log.schema.json:7-22).
Export packaging must fail rather than silently omit explicitly approved optional assets (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/tools/publishers/export_bundle.py:166-171).

MPS request admission requires topic/objective, duration 15-45 seconds, 16:9, and FHP derivation gating; accepted jobs transition queued→processing→completed/failed and expose storyboard, manifest, and artifact paths (/home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:71-85,139-177,196-228).
MPS result retrieval is only valid for completed jobs; otherwise the HTTP API returns conflict rather than a result (/home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/mpve_server.py:47-65).
mps_gaps: No MPS equivalent of OpenMontage's explicit proposal/edit runtime lock and runtime-swap audit exists in the inspected MPVE request/job/result path; MPS carries style and renderer/provider metadata but does not record a locked proposal runtime or compare actual runtime against it.

MPS has no canonical final_review artifact or enforced pass/revise/fail gate. Its completion test can mark a job complete when a mocked renderer writes arbitrary bytes, demonstrating output-path existence rather than media validity (/home/ubuntu/MPS-git/tests/test_mpve.py:23-26,49-64).

MPS does not implement the documented OpenMontage post-render checks for ffprobe validity, four-position visual inspection, audio silence/clipping/mix checks, subtitle presence/coverage, delivery-promise preservation, or runtime-swap detection; production_manifest only lists quality-gate names (/home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/production_manifest.py:64-72).

MPS's RenderResult manifest lacks OpenMontage render_report fields such as format, resolution, codec/audio codec, file size, platform target, final-review reference, and structured verification notes (/home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:35-56; /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/schemas/artifacts/render_report.schema.json:10-60).

MPS has no inspected publish/export step comparable to export_bundle: no packaged metadata/description/tags/chapters/subtitles/thumbnails directory and no schema-validated publish_log for hand-off or platform publication (/home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/tools/publishers/export_bundle.py:179-285 versus /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:196-228).

MPS's fallback assets are recorded in the job result but an SVG-only fallback is forced to failed because no MP4 artifact exists; this is a narrower delivery contract than OpenMontage's explicit artifact/publish status vocabulary (/home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:241-244; /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:206-226).

MPS job state is not restart-safe in the strong sense: JobStore indexes and fingerprints are in memory, and daemon-thread execution is not recovery-oriented; only job.json is written to disk (/home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:131-177,190-194).

MPS exposes a local HTTP API but no authentication, artifact download/streaming route, retention policy, or cleanup policy is shown in the inspected server implementation (/home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/mpve_server.py:22-90).
clean_room_recommendations: Keep MPS independently authored and use OpenMontage only as a behavioral reference: define an MPS-native render report and final review schema rather than copying OpenMontage source, assets, or implementation text.

Add an explicit MPS runtime contract to the request/job artifacts: selected runtime/provider, locked decision rationale, actual runtime, and a boolean plus explanation for any runtime swap or silent downgrade.

Add a post-render QA stage that runs ffprobe, samples at least four representative frames, checks audio presence/silence/clipping, validates subtitles when expected, verifies output duration/resolution/codec, and blocks completion or result presentation on failed checks.
Change MPVE completion from output-file existence to validated media evidence; add tests using malformed bytes and missing/invalid metadata to ensure such jobs fail rather than complete.

Add a repository-native export step that copies the validated MP4 and optional subtitles/thumbnail, writes metadata and chapters, and emits an MPS publish/export record with local-export versus remote-published statuses. Do not imply network publication unless an authenticated provider is actually implemented.

Persist a recoverable job index or rebuild it from job directories on startup, and define idempotency persistence, interrupted-job recovery, artifact retention, and cleanup behavior before treating the HTTP API as production delivery infrastructure.

Expose a safe artifact retrieval or hand-off contract (for example, signed/downloadable paths or an explicitly local-only policy) and document ownership, lifetime, and verification of returned artifact paths.

Preserve MPS-specific pedagogical constraints already present—15-45 seconds, 16:9, learner-interest consent, and FHP derived=true gating—while adding delivery checks as independent quality gates rather than weakening the educational request contract.
